newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds rally after Fed holds rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds rally after Fed holds rates steady.

text.p: Stocks and bonds rallied on Wednesday as the Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady, while the dollar surged to another 40-month peak against the German mark.
The blue-chip Dow Jones industrial average ended up 73.05 points at 7,795.38, which was just below its June 20 record close of 7,796.51.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,837 to 961 on active volume of 526 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks, New York Stock Exchange Composite and Nasdaq Composite indices set record highs.
The fierce rally caught many analysts by surprise, coming as it did after a Fed decision that was nearly universally anticipated on Wall Street.
Initially, investors appeared to shrug off the news, but in the final minutes of the session, a series of buy programmes virtually seized control of the market.

"It's like a game of hot potato where no one wants to get caught holding cash," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "Whether it's mutual funds or brokerage firms or whomever, we've all learned it's no fun to get caught holding cash in a rising market."

The bond market also shot higher, with the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond up 12/32, or $3.75 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.71 percent from 6.74 percent Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

The dollar rose to 1.7540 marks from 1.7471 late on Tuesday, after hitting a third consecutive 40-month peak against the German currency of 1.7550. The dollar fell to 114.47 Japanese yen from 114.93 yen.

After Britain's new Labour government released its first budget, the pound surged to a high of $1.6785 before settling at $1.6755, well above late Tuesday's rate of $1.6588. It also surged to a new five-year peak above 2.94 marks.
Gold prices slid to new four-year lows, dragging down values for other precious metals. Gold for August delivery at the COMEX in New York ended down $2.80 at $332.30 an ounce.

COMEX September silver ended down 3.3 cents at $4.645 an ounce, while October platinum at the New York Mercantile Exchange fell $5.20 an ounce at $406.70 and September palladium closed $1.80 lower at $174.50 an ounce.
Soybean prices fell for a seventh straight day with traders continuing to push prices lower as worries faded about tight supplies ahead of an expected bumper harvest this fall.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybeans for July delivery closed 21 cents a bushel lower at $7.11. That price was down 76 cents or 9.7 percent for the week.
Corn and wheat bucked the selling in soybeans, with July corn closing up 2-1/2 cents a bushel at $2.45-3/4 and July wheat up 1-1/2 cents a bushel at $3.24.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 closed at 4,751.4, up 23.1 points, or 0.49 percent. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,196.42, up 20.90 points, or 0.10 percent.
